sources.title: PostgreSQL range types
sources.independently_observed: tsrange uses timestamps without time zone; tstzrange uses timestamps with time zone. Two-argument constructors use [). Timestamp ranges are continuous. GiST exclusion with && prevents overlap; btree_gist permits scalar equality plus overlap.
sources.applicability: Supports both authority mechanisms and N1's type caveat. Requires correct resource key, interval validity, state scope, and all authoritative writes; cannot protect partitioned independent authorities.
sources.execution: Public source retrieval and reading; no source code, test, API mutation, or executable run.

sources.title: PostgreSQL CREATE TABLE
sources.independently_observed: An exclusion constraint can cover a predicate-selected subset via a partial index. Operators need suitable classes. NOT DEFERRABLE is the default.
sources.applicability: Supports active-state filtering as an implementation choice. Product states, buffers, nullability, and override policy are not furnished by the database.
sources.execution: Public source retrieval and reading; no source code, test, API mutation, or executable run.

sources.title: PostgreSQL date/time
sources.independently_observed: Zoned input is converted to UTC; the original zone is not retained. Unzoned timestamp ignores a zone annotation. Missing zone uses configured TimeZone.
sources.applicability: N1 correctly separates instants from the retained site/display zone. N2 leaves representation to owner choice instead of providing a ready SQL schema.
sources.execution: Public source retrieval and reading; no source code, test, API mutation, or executable run.

sources.title: PostgreSQL SET CONSTRAINTS
sources.independently_observed: Immediate constraints check at statement end; deferred constraints at transaction commit. Nondeferrable constraints stay immediate.
sources.applicability: No candidate claim was treated as proof of a locally executed transaction or deployed schema.
sources.execution: Public source retrieval and reading; no source code, test, API mutation, or executable run.

sources.title: CouchDB conflicts
sources.version_or_snapshot: Stable documentation identifies CouchDB 3.5; mutable path
sources.section_or_symbol: §2.3 conflicts, winner selection and application resolution
sources.independently_observed: Replicas can retain conflicting revisions; deterministic winner selection and ordinary views expose one branch. Applications must find and resolve other branches.
sources.applicability: Both finals correctly distinguish document convergence from physical-tool exclusivity, including separate booking documents with no shared-document conflict.
sources.execution: Public source retrieval and reading; no source code, test, API mutation, or executable run.

sources.title: PouchDB conflicts
sources.section_or_symbol: Eventual conflicts; conflict discovery and resolution
sources.independently_observed: Disconnected updates can succeed locally; conflicts later retain discoverable branches while an arbitrary deterministic winner is returned. Application policy selects resolution.
sources.applicability: Timestamp policy is an application choice, not evidence that losing reservations are physically valid.
sources.execution: Public source retrieval and reading; no source code, test, API mutation, or executable run.

sources.title: PouchDB replication
sources.independently_observed: Multi-master replication permits writes at different nodes. Live replication and retry are distinct options; outage recovery needs explicit retry behavior.
sources.applicability: Supports local capture alternative; not an operationally free or globally exclusive booking system.
sources.execution: Public source retrieval and reading; no source code, test, API mutation, or executable run.

sources.title: InvenTree stock
sources.section_or_symbol: Stock item identity, locations and tracking
sources.independently_observed: Stock records carry part, location, quantity and optional serial identity; locations can be nested. Actor-linked stock history is documented.
sources.applicability: Supports separate serialized custody and quantity/location models. Does not demonstrate a timed lending reservation.

sources.title: InvenTree stock availability
sources.independently_observed: Allocation commits stock while on-hand quantity remains until consumption; available is in-stock minus allocated.
sources.applicability: Order/build quantity commitments are a scoped analogy, not calendar bookings or proof all versions/backends enforce an invariant.
sources.execution: Public source retrieval and reading; no source code, test, API mutation, or executable run.

sources.title: InvenTree units
sources.section_or_symbol: Unit Conversion; case sensitivity; Piece Units; Custom Units
sources.independently_observed: Pint supports compatible conversions. Symbols are case-sensitive; piece/each/dozen/hundred/thousand are supported dimensionless units. Custom dimensionless units use definition 1.
sources.applicability: Supports category-specific units and validation. Integer-only stock is a proposed simple starting policy, not an upstream restriction.

sources.title: InvenTree parts

sources.title: InvenTree stock tracking
sources.section_or_symbol: Tracking entries; deleting stock; Delete Old Entries
sources.independently_observed: Tracking records actor/date/delta; part history can outlive a deleted stock item. Automatic old-entry deletion is disabled by default; the age setting is 365 days when used.
sources.applicability: Both finals keep retention a user policy. Condensing numeric settings does not materially remove the decision.

sources.title: InvenTree bulk data import
sources.section_or_symbol: Safety; permissions; mapping; row validation; updating

sources.applicability: Supports N2's staged-import caveat; proposed target-system rollback remains unimplemented.
